title: Environment values reach the verifier, preview and deploy spawns merged under the wrapper allowlist, and never reach the log
description:
SPIDR grandchild A of task-72b22fcf9da54b3b91dabf5b7392aff1 (architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05), split because the parent measured over the file cap across four subsystems. This row is THE DELIVERY HALF and it is self-contained: it owns the parent's DoD 1, 2 and 5. It carries the parent's dependsOn unchanged (task-d0c63cd8 the store, DONE; task-a2409cba the published commands, BLOCKED at filing).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the plaintext delivery read that child 1 deliberately did NOT export, the merge of environment values into the spawn environment UNDER the existing allowlist, and the spawn half of the canary.

THE PLAINTEXT READ DOES NOT EXIST YET AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts's header states "NO PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION IS EXPORTED FROM THIS MODULE. Delivering values into spawns is a separate concern and a separate row." THIS IS THAT ROW. The primitive exists - `openEnvironmentValue` at apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-cipher.ts:132 - and the read side already opens every seal to derive its fingerprint (environment-projection.ts:89-95) and then DROPS the plaintext. This row adds the one function that returns it, and it should be a NEW focused module so the no-plaintext property of environment-store.ts stays true and greppable.

MERGED UNDER THE ALLOWLIST, NOT AROUND IT. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts` builds a child env from a CLOSED roster: RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS (:14), PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES (:28), and it scrubs every `MOE_*` key (:56). `agentEnvironment()` returns that object. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts:67` reads `options.environment ?? process.env` and passes `env: environment` at :154. Environment values JOIN that construction; a delivery that hands a child `process.env` plus extras destroys the allowlist's whole purpose and would be very hard to notice.

NOTE THE `MOE_*` SCRUB (:56) when choosing the canary variable name: `agentEnvironment` drops every key starting with MOE_, so a canary named `MOE_CANARY_<random>` would be scrubbed by the very construction under test and the arm would pass for the wrong reason. Measure the scrub before naming the canary, and if the parent's suggested name is scrubbed, pick one that is not and say so.

NOT IN SCOPE: the required variable NAMES from the contract and the `.env.example` file (grandchild C, which waits on grandchild B); no UI (parent's child 3).

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: The verifier, preview and deploy spawns receive the environment's variables MERGED UNDER the existing allowlist construction (agent-spawn-environment.ts / verifier-process-runner.ts), not appended to a raw process.env. A test asserts the child's env CONTAINS the delivered variable AND STILL EXCLUDES a host variable outside the allowlist, on the same constructed env - the exclusion arm is what proves the merge did not widen the surface, and without it a passing test is compatible with handing the child everything.

THE SPAWN HALF OF THE CANARY, both directions in ONE test because they pull against each other: set a canary variable to a random value, spawn a verifier, and assert (a) the CHILD SAW the value, read from the CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT and never from the parent's intent, and (b) the value appears NOWHERE in the wrapper log bytes. A delivery that logs what it delivers is the obvious failure and only the pair catches it. The canary name must not be scrubbed by agent-spawn-environment.ts's MOE_ prefix scrub - state which name you used and why it survives.

A plaintext-returning delivery read exists in its OWN module, NOT added to environment-store.ts, whose header states that no plaintext-returning function is exported from it. Assert that property still holds after this row: a grep of environment-store.ts's exports shows no value-returning function.

AN ENVIRONMENT WITH NO VARIABLES SET DELIVERS NOTHING AND REFUSES NOTHING: a spawn with an empty environment must produce a child env byte-identical to what it produces today. Assert the byte-identity against the pre-existing construction, not merely that the spawn succeeded - the verifier ran fine before this feature and must not start depending on it.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: MERGE UNDER THE ALLOWLIST, NEVER AROUND IT. The closed roster exists so a child sees what it needs and nothing else. Never pass `process.env` plus extras, and never widen RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS or PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES to make a test pass.
THE VALUE REACHES THE CHILD AND NOT THE LOG. Assert both, from the child's own output and from the log bytes. One without the other is not evidence.
DELIVERY MUST NOT BECOME A DEPENDENCY: a project with no variables set must spawn exactly as it does today, asserted as byte-identity.

DO NOT ADD A PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION TO environment-store.ts. Its header makes the no-plaintext claim and a canary suite greps it. Put the delivery read in a new focused module with a one-line .js bridge.
Mind the MOE_ scrub at agent-spawn-environment.ts:56 when naming the canary variable, or the arm passes for the wrong reason.
NO required-variable NAMES, NO .env.example, NO UI - those are grandchildren B and C and the parent's child 3.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE. NO EDITS. Three things to settle before writing a line, and the first two change what this row does. (a) THERE ARE TWO ALLOWLIST CONSTRUCTIONS, NOT ONE, and DoD-1 names both files as though they shared one. `agent-spawn-environment.ts:53` `agentEnvironment(source)` filters on `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` OR a `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES` match, scrubs `MOE_*`, then ADDS four keys of its own (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY, MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, NO_PROXY/no_proxy). `verifier-process-runner.ts:377` has its OWN private `runtimeEnvironment(source)` which filters on `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` ALONE - no provider prefixes, no MOE_ scrub, no added keys - and it is the one the verifier spawn actually uses at :68. Confirm both, then decide DELIBERATELY whether delivery is wired once in a shared helper both call, or separately at each site, and say which and why in the step note. Do not assume one construction and wire it in the wrong place. (b) `dependsOn` MAY BE OVERSTATED - CHECK BEFORE WAITING. This row carries `task-a2409cba` (the published `environment.set_variable`/`unset_variable` commands), which is BLOCKED. But `environment-store.ts` EXPORTS `setEnvironmentVariable`:117 and `unsetEnvironmentVariable`:146 directly, so this row's tests can seed values with no command kind at all, and nothing in the five DoD items dispatches a command - this is the delivery READ path, not the operator write path. If you confirm that, say so in a row comment and ask a governor to drop that dependency rather than waiting on a blocked chain; the store row `task-d0c63cd8` is DONE and is the dependency that matters. Do NOT edit dependsOn yourself mid-flight. (c) MEASURE THE MOE_ SCRUB BEFORE NAMING THE CANARY, as the row instructs: `agent-spawn-environment.ts:56` is `if (normalized.startsWith("MOE_") || value === undefined) continue;` - CONFIRMED at plan time, so a `MOE_CANARY_*` name is dropped by the very construction under test and the arm would pass for the wrong reason. Note the verifier's own `runtimeEnvironment` has NO such scrub, so a name can behave differently at the two sites; pick one that survives BOTH and state it. (d) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

THE DELIVERY READ, IN ITS OWN MODULE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-delivery.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (rail 4 asks for the bridge by name; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). THIS MODULE EXISTS SO A PROPERTY STAYS TRUE: `environment-store.ts`'s header states that NO PLAINTEXT-RETURNING FUNCTION IS EXPORTED FROM IT, and a canary suite greps that file. Adding the read there would falsify a claim another test depends on - which is why child 1 deliberately left this out. Export ONE function returning the environment's variables as plaintext `{name: value}`. Build it on `openEnvironmentValue` (environment-cipher.ts:132), whose docblock records the property to preserve: a wrong credential, a flipped byte, a replayed salt and a swapped tag ALL land on AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with NO BYTES RELEASED, because GCM verifies before it yields. Do not soften that - a delivery that returns partial plaintext on a tampered seal is worse than one that refuses. `environment-projection.ts:89-95` already opens every seal to derive a fingerprint and then DROPS the plaintext; read it and follow the same opening path rather than inventing a second one. DECIDE AND STATE what the read does when ONE seal of several fails to open: refusing the whole delivery is defensible, delivering the rest is defensible, silently skipping is not. Say which and why in the docblock - a spawn that quietly receives three of four variables is the kind of thing that is diagnosed at 2am. Write the module's header to state its one job and to name why it is not in environment-store.ts, so the next reader does not tidy it back in.

THE MERGE, AND THE THING THAT MAKES 'UNDER THE ALLOWLIST' AMBIGUOUS. Wire delivery into the spawn environment at the site(s) step 1(a) settled. READ THIS FIRST: an operator's variable names are ARBITRARY (`DATABASE_URL`, `STRIPE_KEY`), so they are NOT in `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` and do NOT match `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES`. Passing them through `agentEnvironment(source)` or `runtimeEnvironment(source)` DROPS EVERY ONE OF THEM - the closed roster is doing exactly its job. So 'merged UNDER the allowlist' cannot mean 'passed through the filter'; it means APPLIED TO THE OBJECT THE FILTER RETURNS, after the allowlist construction has done its work. A worker who reads it the other way gets a test where the delivered variable never arrives, and the tempting next move is to widen `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` - WHICH RAIL 1 FORBIDS IN THOSE WORDS. Never widen either roster to make a test pass. The shape is: build the allowlisted env exactly as today, then overlay the delivered variables onto that result. DECIDE THE COLLISION RULE AND STATE IT: what happens when a delivered variable has the same name as an allowlisted host variable (`PATH`, say, or `HOME`). An operator variable silently overriding PATH is a foot-gun; refusing it, or refusing to overwrite an allowlisted key, is defensible. Pick one, write it in the docblock, and give it a test arm - this is the kind of decision that is invisible until it breaks a spawn. KEEP THE HOST FILES SMALL: verifier-process-runner.ts is 395 lines against a 400 cap - FIVE lines of headroom - so the merge logic goes in the new module and the call site is one line. agent-spawn-environment.ts is 83 lines and has room, but the same rule applies: one construction, called from both sites, beats two copies that drift.

THE TESTS, AND THE CANARY IS ONE TEST FOR A REASON. (1) DoD-2, THE CANARY, BOTH DIRECTIONS IN ONE TEST because they pull against each other: set a variable to a random value, spawn a verifier, and assert (a) THE CHILD SAW IT, read from THE CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT - never from the parent's intent, never from the env object you constructed, because asserting the object you just built proves only that you built it; and (b) the value appears NOWHERE in the wrapper log bytes. Split into two tests, each half can pass while the other fails and nobody notices; together they are the property. Use the name step 1(c) proved survives the MOE_ scrub at BOTH sites, and say in a comment why that name and not `MOE_CANARY_*`. (2) DoD-1's PAIR, and the exclusion half is the load-bearing one: on the SAME constructed env, assert the delivered variable IS present AND a host variable outside the allowlist is STILL ABSENT. Without the exclusion arm, a passing test is compatible with having handed the child `process.env` plus extras - which is the failure rail 1 exists to prevent and is very hard to notice in review. (3) DoD-4, BYTE-IDENTITY: with an environment that has NO variables set, the constructed child env is byte-identical to what the pre-existing construction produces. Assert equality against the OLD construction's output, not merely that the spawn succeeded - the verifier ran fine before this feature and must not start depending on it. This is the arm that catches an unconditional overlay that adds an empty object, a key with an undefined value, or a reordered object. (4) DoD-3: a grep of `environment-store.ts`'s exports shows no value-returning function - assert it as source text the way `goal-publish.test.tsx` pins its no-localStorage property, so the claim in that file's header stays true and greppable. (5) The collision rule from step 3 and the partial-open decision from step 2, each with an arm asserting the behaviour you chose.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. MIXED: the delivery module, its bridge and its test are NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is BLIND to them - SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), proved in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The two spawn files and the verifier test are TRACKED and take an empty `git diff`. Say which proof applies to which path. THREE DRILLS: (i) THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST - make the merge hand the child `process.env` plus the delivered variables instead of overlaying the allowlisted object. The DELIVERY arm still passes; the EXCLUSION arm from DoD-1 must go RED. Quote it. That pair is the only thing standing between this feature and a silently widened process surface, and if the exclusion arm stays green it is not testing what it claims. (ii) Log the delivered value on the delivery path and confirm the canary's log-bytes half reds - a delivery that logs what it delivers is the obvious failure and this proves the arm sees it. (iii) Make the empty-environment path overlay an empty object unconditionally and confirm the DoD-4 byte-identity arm reds; if it stays green it was asserting success rather than identity. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence here - vitest.config.ts:32 has no `apps/**`. `wc -l` verifier-process-runner.ts before and after and quote both: it was 395 against a 400 cap at plan time, so it has FIVE lines of headroom and crossing it is a rejection. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: a delivered variable whose value contains a newline or a NUL (the verifier spawns with `shell: true` at :151 - what does a value with a shell metacharacter do there, and is that this row's problem or a finding for the owner); a variable named `PATH` (the collision rule); an environment whose seal fails to open mid-delivery; the value reaching a CRASH path's output as well as the log; whether the delivered value can appear in a receipt, an error message or a stack trace, not only the log; two spawns racing the same delivery read. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: which of the TWO allowlist constructions you wired, and whether you unified them or wired both, with the reason; the canary variable name and why it survives the MOE_ scrub at both sites; the collision rule and the partial-open rule, both as chosen behaviour rather than as accidents; drill (i)'s red verbatim; the `wc -l` before/after for verifier-process-runner.ts; and whether you confirmed the `task-a2409cba` dependency is unnecessary, so a governor can drop it.

THREE MEASURED FINDINGS, ONE ACTIONABLE NOW BY A GOVERNOR. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 5 files (2 new).

## 1. "Merged UNDER the allowlist" is ambiguous, and the obvious reading is broken

An operator's variable names are arbitrary — `DATABASE_URL`, `STRIPE_KEY`. They are **not** in `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` and do **not** match `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES`. So passing them through `agentEnvironment(source)` or `runtimeEnvironment(source)` **drops every one of them** — the closed roster doing exactly its job.

The merge must be applied to the object the filter **returns**, not to its input. A worker who reads it the other way gets a test where nothing arrives, and the tempting next move is widening the roster — which rail 1 forbids in those words. Named in step 3.

## 2. There are TWO allowlist constructions, and DoD-1 names both files as if they shared one

```
agent-spawn-environment.ts:53   agentEnvironment()     key set OR provider prefix,
                                                       scrubs MOE_*, ADDS 4 keys
verifier-process-runner.ts:377  runtimeEnvironment()   PRIVATE. key set ALONE.
                                                       no prefixes, no scrub, no additions
```

And `:68` shows the verifier spawn uses the **private** one. Wiring delivery into `agentEnvironment` and assuming the verifier is covered leaves that spawn undelivered while the test passes. Step 1 makes the worker confirm both and decide deliberately whether to unify them.

**Consequence for the canary:** the `MOE_*` scrub exists at one site and not the other, so a name can behave differently at each. The plan requires a name that survives **both**. (Scrub confirmed at `agent-spawn-environment.ts:56`; the row's warning is correct.)

## 3. The `dependsOn` on task-a2409cba (BLOCKED) looks unnecessary — governor call

`environment-store.ts` **exports** `setEnvironmentVariable`:117 and `unsetEnvironmentVariable`:146, so this row's tests can seed values with no command kind at all. None of the five DoD items dispatches a command — this is the delivery **read** path, not the operator write path. The dependency that matters, `task-d0c63cd8` (the store), is **DONE**.

If that holds, dropping `task-a2409cba` makes this row claimable now instead of gated behind a blocked chain. I did not edit `dependsOn` myself: the row is claimed for PLANNING and a dependency change while another architect's chain is mid-flight is a governor's call. Step 1 has the worker confirm and raise it.

## Two behaviours the row leaves undecided, and neither should be an accident

- **A delivered variable named `PATH`.** Silently overriding an allowlisted host value is a foot-gun; refusing it is defensible. Pick one, document it, test it.
- **One seal of several failing to open.** Refuse the whole delivery, or deliver the rest — both defensible. **Silently skipping is not**: a spawn quietly receiving three of four variables is diagnosed at 2am.

## Constraints and drills

`verifier-process-runner.ts` is **395 lines against a 400 cap** — five lines of headroom, so the merge logic goes in the new module and the call site is one line.

The row's load-bearing drill is (i): make the merge hand the child `process.env` plus extras. The **delivery** arm still passes; the **exclusion** arm must go red. That pair is the only thing between this feature and a silently widened process surface — and if the exclusion arm stays green it is not testing what it claims.

One thing the canary does not cover: the log is not the only leak surface. A value can reach a receipt, an error message, a stack trace or a crash path's output. The adversarial pass looks at those.

planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE MERGE READ THE WRONG WAY DROPS EVERY VARIABLE, and the tempting fix is the one rail 1 forbids. Operator names are arbitrary and therefore not on either closed roster; passing them through the filter deletes them. Overlay onto the filter's OUTPUT. Never widen `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` or `PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES` to make an arm pass.

SECOND - WIRING ONE CONSTRUCTION AND ASSUMING THE OTHER. `agentEnvironment` and `runtimeEnvironment` are different functions with different rules, and the verifier uses the private one. Delivery wired only into the first leaves the verifier spawn undelivered while a test against the first passes.

THIRD - THE EXCLUSION ARM IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF DoD-1. Asserting only that the delivered variable arrived is compatible with having handed the child `process.env` plus extras. Drill (i) reproduces exactly that and requires the exclusion arm to red.

FOURTH - ASSERTING THE OBJECT YOU BUILT PROVES NOTHING. DoD-2 says read from the CHILD'S OWN OUTPUT; a test that inspects the constructed env object proves only that it was constructed. And splitting the canary into two tests lets either half rot unnoticed - it is one test because the two halves pull against each other.

FIFTH - THE MOE_ SCRUB WOULD MAKE THE CANARY PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON at one of the two sites. Measure, then name.

SIXTH - DELIVERY MUST NOT BECOME A DEPENDENCY. An unconditional overlay that adds an empty object, an undefined-valued key, or a reordered object breaks byte-identity for a project with no variables. Assert identity against the OLD construction's output, not spawn success.

SEVENTH - TWO BEHAVIOURS ARE UNDECIDED AND MUST NOT BE ACCIDENTS: what a delivered variable named `PATH` does to an allowlisted host value, and what happens when one seal of several fails to open. Silent skipping is the wrong answer to the second in every case - a spawn quietly receiving three of four variables is diagnosed at 2am.

EIGHTH - FIVE LINES OF HEADROOM in verifier-process-runner.ts (395/400). The merge logic belongs in the new module; the call site is one line.

NINTH - THE LOG IS NOT THE ONLY LEAK SURFACE. A value can reach a receipt, an error message, a stack trace or a crash path's output. The canary covers the log; the adversarial pass must look at the others.

TENTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles, including the new module and its bridge.
